fact: ITWeb Africa reports Cameroon currently operates about 12,000 km of terrestrial fibre-optic network plus about 812 km of overhead fibre on electricity poles, all managed by state operator Camtel; it does not list regions served. As of date is the article's published date.

fact: NewsWatch states that CAMTEL owns and operates Cameroon's national fibre-optic backbone of over 15,000 km; the article gives no regions or towns and no in-service date, so the date is the article's own (2026-07-27).

NewsWatch states that CAMTEL leases capacity on its national fibre-optic backbone to private mobile network operators, while holding exclusive rights over the backbone itself; the date is the article's own (2026-07-27).
The deal record puts CAMTEL's existing national fibre at about 12,000 km terrestrial plus about 812 km overhead on electricity poles, as reported on 2026-03-09; it names no regions or towns.
Reporting ART's 2024 Annual Observatory, TechAfrica News says transport, mainly by the incumbent CAMTEL, relies on a national fibre optic network of nearly 12,000 km; no regions or towns are named.

ITWeb Africa reports that in 2023 the government transferred to Camtel an overhead fibre-optic network of about 812km on electricity poles along the southern interconnected grid, which serves major cities including Douala and Yaounde, adding to Camtel's terrestrial fibre network of about 12,000km.
Camtel's national fibre-optic backbone, about 12,000 km, serves all ten regional capitals and 51 of 58 divisional capitals, according to the ART report quoted by Ecomatin.
The ART report says Camtel's transport network revenue rose with demand for bandwidth from mobile operators, ISPs and businesses.
OBS-CC says over 12,000 km of fibre form the national backbone run by Camtel, linking the regions to each other and to the coast, with published estimates up to nearly 16,000 km.
OBS-CC says Camtel carries Chad's traffic to the sea cables over its fibre, and that a 15 May 2025 deal settling Sotel Tchad's debt raised that capacity to over 100 Gbit/s.
CAMTEL's 2026 product sheet says its national fibre-optic network of nearly 10,000 km covers the whole territory and carries its inter-city leased lines on the national backbone.
CAMTEL's 2026 product sheet offers operators and ISPs inter-city leased lines (LLI) on its national backbone, IP transit and cross-connection, as wholesale products.

Cameroon's telecoms regulator ART says its audit, nearly complete, of the 112 sections of CAMTEL's national fibre-optic network, which link operators' sites across regions, departments and districts, found significant degradation with recurrent cuts and partly unavailable sections.
